data_status: STRICT MODE: this dataset contains only values that were compared with, or ingested directly from, retrieved sources: JPL (SSD, SBDB, NHATS), NASA (NSSDC fact sheets and mission catalog, Small Spacecraft SoA report 2026, SLS page, Apollo 11 press kit, NTRS papers, data.nasa.gov), ULA, ESA, NIST, and the Launch Library 2 aggregator. Records carry source_authority/confidence where the source is an aggregator or vendor-reported compilation. Recalled, estimated and fictional values (optimizer catalog, costs, engine/vehicle specs without a retrievable source, the user-supplied SpaceX table) are not included. Derived values are computed only from verified inputs and are labelled derived.

record.name: Mars Hand Lens Imager (MAHLI)
record.description: The primary objective of the MArs Hand Lens Imager (MAHLI) is to acquire images at high magnification (hand lens scale) of chosen rock and regolith targets. The high magnification enables study of the petrography and mineralogy of the rocks. MAHLI images are also used for identification of samples for other instruments, such as APXS, CheMin, or SAM. MAHLI is mounted on the turret at the end of the robotic arm. The imager can focus at distances between 20.4 mm and infinity, with a resolution as high as 13.9 microns/pixel. At 25 mm the field of view is 34 degrees diagonal with an effective focal length of 18.3 mm at f/9.8. At infinity, the field of view is 39.4 degrees diagonal with effective focal length of 21.3 mm at f/8.5. The instrument bandpass is 380 to 680 nm. For more detailed information, see: http://msl-scicorner.jpl.nasa.gov/Instruments/MAHLI/
